newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-BECKER CANCELS BOSTON TRIP AFTER FRIEND DIES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER CANCELS BOSTON TRIP AFTER FRIEND DIES.

text.p: Boris Becker has cancelled his trip to Boston, where he was due to play on Tuesday, after the death of adviser and close friend Axel Meyer-Woelden, German media reported.
Meyer-Woelden, one of Germany's most influential sports managers, died of liver cancer on Monday in Munich. He was 56.
Becker, who had close personal and business ties with Meyer-Woelden, decided not to go to Boston, where he was scheduled to play Brazilian Fernando Meligeni on Tuesday night.
The 29-year-old former world number one was planning to make his comeback after a four-week injury break at the U.S. Pro Tennis Championships, where he was seeded fourth.

Popular daily Bild said Becker would also miss the U.S. Open starting on Monday in New York but sports agency Sid were more cautious, saying his participation was in doubt. Becker was not available for comment.
Becker, who made an emotional farewell to Wimbledon last July, was expected to make his last appearance in a Grand Slam event at the U.S. Open.
He confirmed recently that the end of his career was nearing but added he would play a few more tournaments next year and make himself available for Davis Cup duties with Germany.
